interpretations: Overall average is the mean of the per-telescope averages, so each telescope counts equally. This is the reading the question states.
Overall average is the mean of all non-null modindex values across all signals, so telescopes with more signals count more.
Overall average is the mean of the per-telescope averages, but only over telescopes that have at least one non-null modindex. Telescopes with all-null values are excluded from the group mean.
Overall average is the mean of the per-telescope averages, with all-null telescopes included as zero.
"Ignoring missing values" means skipping NULL modindex values when averaging. Zero values are kept.
"Ignoring missing values" also treats zero or sentinel modindex values as missing.
"Each telescope" means only the distinct telescref values present in the signals table. Telescopes in the telescopes table with no signals are not included.
"Each telescope" means all telescopes in the telescopes table, including those with no signals.
"How much it exceeds the overall average" is the absolute difference: telescope average minus overall average.
"How much it exceeds the overall average" is the percentage difference: (telescope average − overall average) / overall average × 100.
"Its average as a ratio to the group average" is the telescope average divided by the overall average.
"Its average as a ratio to the group average" is expressed as a percentage, i.e. ratio × 100.
"Above the overall average" is a strict greater-than comparison. Telescopes exactly equal to the overall average are excluded.
"Above the overall average" is a greater-than-or-equal comparison.
"Top 10 by that ratio, highest first" means ordering by the ratio descending and limiting to 10 rows. Ordering by ratio is the same as ordering by average or by excess.
Ties at the 10th position are cut off arbitrarily by the limit.
Ties at the 10th position are all included.
"Without rounding" means returning the full-precision values, with no ROUND or formatting applied.
The output columns are telescope reference, average modulation index, excess over the overall average, and ratio. Column order and naming follow the question.
The output also includes the overall average as an extra column.
If fewer than 10 telescopes are above the average, return only those that qualify.
Missing interpretations:

"Ratio to the group average" is computed as the telescope average divided by the overall average, but the ratio is not returned as a separate rounded or percentage column. The ratio itself is the ordering key.
Telescopes whose signals have a NULL `telescref` are excluded. `telescref` is NOT NULL, so none exist.
The per-telescope average is taken over signals grouped by the `telescref` string exactly as stored. Case or whitespace variants of the same telescope are not merged.
Ties in the ratio are broken by telescope reference as a secondary sort order, to make the ordering deterministic.
The excess over the overall average is returned as a ratio minus 1 (a fractional excess), not as an absolute difference or a percentage.
